correctness.rationale: For any n>=3, connected feasible allocations form a convex domain where trace inverse of the mean-zero Laplacian is strictly convex; edge-to-Laplacian injectivity proves unrestricted uniqueness and graph automorphisms force two conductance classes. Both classes must be positive. Fourier diagonalization gives one zero mode, the identity sum 1/(4 sin^2)= (n^2-1)/12, and the exact scalar derivative condition. The Poisson resolvent sum is exact; compactness bounds show t_n is Theta(n^-2/3), uniform convergence on compact scaled ratios identifies s_*=(18P^2/Q^2)^(1/3), and the limiting minimum equals Qs_*/(4B). Verifier gave 57 successful grouped checks including exact symbolic trace identities and unrestricted SLSQP comparisons. No finite experiment is used to prove the asymptotic.

value.rationale: The priced prism is a natural two-rail network with many redundant rungs. The result answers a genuine allocation question at every finite circumference, proves positive but asymptotically vanishing rung expenditure, and identifies a nontrivial fractional n^-2/3 boundary layer with a sharp second-order objective coefficient. The equal-price optimal-vs-uniform asymptotic ratio 2/3 gives a structural, quantitative design consequence. This is not a one-off enumeration, renaming, or generic application of known convexity: the critical exponent and coefficient require the periodic Green-function singularity and a scaling argument.
